_meta.note: Official-source tracking (formerly review_triggers here) moved to upstream-sources-registry's assets/sources.json. The two internal (non-official-source) triggers this used to list -- skill-development/references/size-limits.md and skill-reviewer's severity-tier logic -- were not migrated there; they remain R20 Duplicate Fact Sweep's job, unrelated to external source tracking. See upstream-sources-registry's references/migration-notes.md for the full mapping.

R1_language_english_only.description: All frontmatter fields and body content must be in English

R2_reference_english_required.description: Every references/ file must have an English primary version

R3_reference_multilingual.description: Reference files may have language variant files alongside the English primary

R4_naming_kebab_case.description: All component identifiers must use lowercase kebab-case

R5_frontmatter_no_nonstandard_fields.description: Skill and agent frontmatter must not include command-only or unsupported fields
R5_frontmatter_no_nonstandard_fields.platform_behavior_claim_note: This rule's AskUserQuestion-in-allowed-tools sub-clause is a specific, falsifiable claim about current Claude Code tool-permission mechanics (not a naming/formatting convention this repo controls) -- it was wrong for an unknown duration until corrected 2026-07-27 against code.claude.com/docs/en/skills, and had propagated to 9 other files including a live-enforcing hook before the error was caught. See upstream-sources-registry's periodic sweep -- rules tagged platform_behavior_claim: true should be prioritized first, since they can go stale the moment the platform changes with no local signal that anything is wrong.

config.agent_nonfunctional_fields_note: Schema-accepted but not honored for plugin-scoped agents (upstream security restriction) -- flag as ADVISORY, not REQUIRED, since the field doesn't break validation, it silently does nothing

R6_tool_scoping_least_privilege.description: allowed-tools may be space-separated, comma-separated, or a YAML list; apply principle of least privilege

R7_no_emoji_in_structure.description: No emoji in section headings, frontmatter fields, or procedural step labels

R8_description_multiline_syntax.description: Descriptions over 80 characters must use >- YAML block scalar syntax

R9_no_hardcoded_credentials.description: No API keys, tokens, passwords, or secrets in any plugin file

R10_reference_file_naming.description: Reference files use descriptive, specific, kebab-case topic names (max 40 chars, no generic names)

R12_code_block_language_specifier.description: All fenced code blocks must include a language identifier (```yaml, ```json, ```bash)

R13_skillmd_line_limit.description: SKILL.md total line count — tiered severity by threshold (see references/size-rules.md)

R14_references_one_level_deep.description: No nested subdirectories in references/ — only references/<file>.md is valid

R15_no_human_documentation_files.description: No README.md, CHANGELOG.md, INSTALLATION.md, or similar human-facing docs in skill directories

R16_progressive_disclosure_order.description: Quick Start section must appear before detailed workflow or reference sections in SKILL.md

R17_no_bare_urls.description: All hyperlinks must use named reference syntax — text in brackets, URL in parentheses

R18_code_block_line_limit.description: Inline fenced code block line count — tiered severity by threshold (see references/size-rules.md)

R19_canonical_path_resolution.description: Resolve the target component's actual file path and verify no duplicate/shadow copy of the same named component exists in another scope (project, plugin, or user skill directories)

R20_duplicate_fact_sweep.description: When a canonical enum, threshold, or field value changes, sweep the plugin tree for other occurrences of the old value in sibling files and flag any not updated

R21_skill_description_size.description: SKILL.md description/when_to_use/combined length — tiered severity by threshold (see references/size-rules.md)

R22_argument_frontmatter_consistency.description: argument-hint/arguments frontmatter must match $ARGUMENTS/$N/$name usage in the body (see references/argument-consistency.md)

R23_external_reference_policy.description: External references (companies, GitHub orgs, marketplaces, plugins, skills, repositories) must be classified whitelist/blacklist; unclassified and broken references are flagged (see references/external-reference-policy.md)

R24_allowed_programming_languages.description: Only Python, Bash, and JavaScript/TypeScript are allowed as programming/scripting languages anywhere in the plugin (script files and embedded fenced code blocks); Ruby is banned explicitly; every other language is banned by default-deny since the whitelist is closed

config.notes: whitelist_extensions/whitelist_language_tags form a closed allowlist — a script file or fenced-block tag not on this list is banned by default-deny, not just the languages named in 'banned'. 'banned' exists to name explicitly-prohibited languages (Ruby) even though the closed whitelist already implies the same rejection, so the prohibition is visible without inferring it from an absence.

R25_unplanned_overhead_disclosure.description: A skill/pipeline whose actual execution deviates from a documented quick/fast/bounded phase (extra retries, debugging detours, an unplanned fallback) must disclose this to the user in plain language, not fold it silently into a clean final result

R26_expensive_action_optin.description: A skill/agent step capable of triggering per-item nested LLM/subprocess calls, whole-surface re-verification, or heavy multi-agent dispatch must gate that action behind an explicit AskUserQuestion decision rather than defaulting to always running it

R27_component_naming_grammatical_form.description: Skills, agents, and commands should follow their documented grammatical form (skill: noun/gerund, agent: role noun, command: verb-first) per naming-conventions.md's Component-Type Conventions table -- interpretive, never blocking

languages.notes: Add or remove codes in 'additional' to control which language variants are permitted

color.notes: magenta is no longer listed in current platform docs; flag as deprecated, not invalid

permissionMode.notes: manual is an alias for default, introduced in Claude Code v2.1.200+

structured_output.notes: Canonical closed-enum value list for the 'action' field in any plugin-devkit reviewer agent's Structured Output Mode findings[]. Loaded in Step 1 by every reviewer agent with a Structured Output Mode (rather than hardcoded inline) so R20's Duplicate Fact Sweep can catch drift if a future agent copies it inline instead of loading it. 'per_agent_extensions' lists agent-specific additional action values kept out of the shared base list because they only make sense for that agent's domain (e.g. rule-reviewer's split_rule/move_to_skill mirror literal recommendation terms already used in its own prose; hook-reviewer's 6 values cover the script/config-level fixes — exit code, file filtering, settings.json registration, security, error handling, output limits — that the generic frontmatter/reference-file-oriented base list was never designed for; activation-reviewer's 5 values cover cross-component trigger-overlap remediations — narrowing a description's scope, adding an explicit exclusion, merging or splitting components, or adding a file/keyword trigger hint — none of which map to a single-file structural edit the base enum was designed for; skilldir-reviewer's 2 values cover merging near-duplicate content found across a skill's own non-SKILL.md files, and flattening a nested reference file up one level for R14 — distinct from move_to_references, which moves content INTO references/ from elsewhere, not sideways within it) — an agent with an entry here loads the base list plus its own extension, not a replacement. claudemd-reviewer's YAML 'rule' field is a separate, fully domain-specific enum (CLAUDE.md violation categories) and intentionally does not use this list at all.

suggested_edit_field.applies_to: findings[] entries, alongside the existing free-text 'fix' field
suggested_edit_field.notes: Optional. Populate ONLY when the fix reduces to a single, unambiguous literal find-replace within one file — the exact old_string must appear verbatim and only once in the target file (the same uniqueness constraint the Edit tool itself enforces), so a caller can paste it directly into an Edit call without further judgment. Never populate this for a fix that requires narrative judgment, spans multiple files, or needs surrounding-context disambiguation — leave 'fix' as prose-only for those, same as before this field existed. This field is additive: agents that don't implement it are unaffected, and 'fix' remains required on every finding regardless of whether 'suggested_edit' is also present.
